# Use subagent-design

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Decompose a task into an orchestrator and subagents — one-mission role cards with typed output contracts, a topology (pipeline / parallel / judge panel) chosen with a reason, context-isolation rationale, and a verification stage that is never a generator.

**Reach for it when** the user wants to fan work out across multiple agents, design a multi-agent workflow or orchestration, or asks "should this be one agent or several".

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install subagent-design                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install subagent-design --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install subagent-design --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the AI engineering pack: [`--pack ai-engineering`](../packs/use-the-ai-engineering-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "Should this task be one agent or several?"
- "Design a multi-agent workflow to audit all our repos"
- "My agent fan-out produces mush — help me add contracts and verification"
- "Pipeline or parallel for this multi-stage agent job?"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Design the loop with exit criteria and human gates for this automation"
- "Set a token budget for our agent workflows"
- "Run a council review on this architecture decision"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use subagent-design".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **The fan-out is justified by one of the three reasons, by name** — or the plan says "one agent" and means it.
- **Every mission is one sentence with no "and".** Two jobs, two cards.
- **Every output contract is typed.** A reader could write the JSON schema from the card.
- **Isolation lines are explicit** — each card says what the agent is denied and why.
- **The topology has its reason attached**, and any barrier names the cross-item dependency that earns it.
- **Verification is adversarial and separate** — never the generator, never "the orchestrator double-checks".
- **The budget line exists** — per-agent tier + fleet cap, sourced or tagged.

## Use something else when

- Designing the loop that wraps the fan-out (caps, gates, exits) — `agent-loop-design`
- Setting the spend policy — `agent-budget`
- Running a multi-perspective review right now — `council-review` is the panel, ready-made
- Implementing one story — `feature-implement-loop`
